--- title: "Lorem ipsum: a Quarto field notebook" author: Max Thomasberger subtitle: "An executable R publishing showcase" description: "A public design showcase for typography, executable R, figures, citations, and interactive charts." date: "2026-10-26" categories: [showcase] draft: false bibliography: references.bib number-sections: true body-classes: article-tufte reference-location: margin citation-location: margin format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 2 toc-location: body mermaid: theme: neutral code-fold: true code-summary: "Show R code" code-tools: true code-line-numbers: true code-annotations: below citations-hover: true footnotes-hover: true lightbox: true execute: message: false warning: false --- ::: {.callout-note} ## Design showcase This page is a public design and publishing demonstration for feedback, using placeholder prose and entirely synthetic data. It is not a finished research article and makes no investment claims. The examples execute locally with R, knitr, ggplot2, DT, and Plotly. ::: ## Prose and structure {#sec-prose} Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Integer posuere erat a ante venenatis dapibus posuere velit aliquet. Donec ullamcorper nulla non metus auctor fringilla. Aenean lacinia bibendum nulla sed consectetur. **Strong emphasis**, *quiet emphasis*, ~~deleted text~~, and `inline code` can sit beside ordinary prose. A footnote adds a small aside without breaking the paragraph.[^placeholder] [^placeholder]: Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. This footnote demonstrates the reading experience; it is not a research reference. > Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed posuere > consectetur est at lobortis. A research note : A short definition can live directly in the article. A computational article : Prose, source code, and evaluated output travel together. - Introduce the question. - Show enough code to reproduce the calculation. - Explain what the outputs mean. 1. Prepare inputs. 2. Compute a result. 3. Review the evidence. ### An aside in the margin ::: {.column-margin} **Margin note.** Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. Quarto can place short annotations beside the main text on wide screens. ::: Cras mattis consectetur purus sit amet fermentum. Maecenas faucibus mollis interdum. Nulla vitae elit libero, a pharetra augue. Praesent commodo cursus magna, vel scelerisque nisl consectetur et. ## Executable R and inline results {#sec-computation} This paragraph contains evaluated R: the example has 252 observations, with a sample mean of -0.0244. The values are computed from the same data used in @fig-path and @tbl-summary. R itself is documented by @R. Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Vestibulum id ligula porta felis euismod semper. Etiam porta sem malesuada magna mollis euismod. Curabitur blandit tempus porttitor. ### Folded code and tabular output The disclosure below contains executable code. The page's **Code** menu can show or hide all code and display the article source. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} knitr::kable(head(research, 6), digits = 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} | day| innovation| path| |---:|----------:|-----:| | 1| 1.371| 1.371| | 2| -0.565| 0.806| | 3| 0.363| 1.169| | 4| 0.633| 1.802| | 5| 0.404| 2.207| | 6| -0.106| 2.100| ::: ::: ### Annotated code The explanations stay below the code on every screen size. Select a numbered explanation to highlight its line; copy the code using the separate toolbar. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} centered <- research$innovation - mean(research$innovation) # <1> round(sd(centered), 3) # <2> ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.974 ``` ::: ::: 1. Subtract the sample mean from every simulated observation. 2. Compute the sample standard deviation and print a compact result. ## Figures and cross-references {#sec-figures} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(ggplot2) ggplot(research, aes(day, path)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = palette$muted, linewidth = 0.4) + geom_line(colour = plot_accent, linewidth = 0.7) + labs(x = "Observation", y = "Cumulative sum") + theme_blechturm("light") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![An accumulated sequence of simulated normal draws.](index_files/figure-html/fig-path-1.png){#fig-path fig-alt='A navy line showing the cumulative sum of 252 simulated normal observations.' width=768} ::: ::: @fig-path is numbered automatically. Click the image to try the lightbox. A cross-reference such as @sec-computation also follows the section if it moves. ### Side-by-side figures ::: {#fig-diagnostics .cell layout-ncol="2"} ```{.r .cell-code} par( bg = paper, fg = ink, col.axis = ink, col.lab = ink, mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1) ) hist(research$innovation, breaks = 20, col = plot_accent, border = paper, main = "", xlab = "Innovation", ylab = "Count") qqnorm(research$innovation, main = "", pch = 16, cex = 0.6, col = plot_accent) qqline(research$innovation, col = ink) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Distribution](index_files/figure-html/fig-diagnostics-1.png){#fig-diagnostics-1 fig-alt='A histogram of simulated normal observations.' width=384} ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Normal Q-Q plot](index_files/figure-html/fig-diagnostics-2.png){#fig-diagnostics-2 fig-alt='A normal quantile plot of the same observations, with a reference line.' width=384} ::: Two diagnostic views of the synthetic observations. ::: Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Duis mollis, est non commodo luctus, nisi erat porttitor ligula, eget lacinia odio sem nec elit. ## A shared plotting palette {#sec-plot-themes} The ledgr logo supplies the navy, blue, orange, and gray color families. Orange is darkened for contrast on a light background, while the blues are lightened for dark mode. The synthetic signals deliberately overlap; line styles and labels identify them independently of color. These examples demonstrate the layout, not research findings.
Navy Blue Orange Graphite
### ggplot2: the static figure This figure switches between two pre-rendered images when you change the site's light/dark setting. R runs at render time, never in the browser. ::: {.plot-light} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} signal_plot + scale_colour_blechturm("light") + theme_blechturm("light") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/themed-ggplot-light-1.png){fig-alt='Four synthetic signals A through D, distinguished by navy, blue, orange and gray colors and different line patterns, on a light background.' width=768} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.plot-dark} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} signal_plot + scale_colour_blechturm("dark") + theme_blechturm("dark") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/themed-ggplot-dark-1.png){fig-alt='The same four synthetic signals with lighter navy, blue, orange and gray colors and different line patterns, on a charcoal background.' width=768} ::: ::: ::: ### Deliberate emphasis {#sec-plot-focus} This version deliberately emphasizes **A**, using the same navy accent. B, C, and D use graphite and retain their distinct line styles. This treatment suits a question about one focal series; the full palette above gives each series its own color. ::: {.plot-light} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p <- blechturm_palette("light") focus_colours <- setNames(rep(p$muted, 4), levels(signals$series)) focus_colours["A"] <- p$series[[1]] signal_plot + scale_colour_manual(values = focus_colours) + theme_blechturm("light") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/focused-ggplot-light-1.png){fig-alt='Four overlapping synthetic signals; A is navy and the three comparison series are gray, with different line styles, on a light background.' width=768} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.plot-dark} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p <- blechturm_palette("dark") focus_colours <- setNames(rep(p$muted, 4), levels(signals$series)) focus_colours["A"] <- p$series[[1]] signal_plot + scale_colour_manual(values = focus_colours) + theme_blechturm("dark") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/focused-ggplot-dark-1.png){fig-alt='The same overlapping signals; A is light blue and comparison series are gray, with different line styles, on a charcoal background.' width=768} ::: ::: ::: ### Plotly: the interactive companion Hover to inspect a value, drag to zoom, double-click to reset, or click a legend entry to hide a series. The same page theme switch updates chart backgrounds, text, and trace colors without recomputing the data. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p <- plotly::plot_ly() series_names <- levels(signals$series) line_styles <- c("solid", "dash", "dot", "dashdot") for (i in seq_along(series_names)) { rows <- signals$series == series_names[i] p <- plotly::add_trace( p, x = signals$day[rows], y = signals$value[rows], name = series_names[i], type = "scatter", mode = "lines", line = list(color = palette$series[[i]], dash = line_styles[i], width = 2), hovertemplate = "Observation %{x}
Signal %{y:.2f}%{fullData.name}" ) } p <- plotly::layout(p, xaxis = list(title = "Observation"), yaxis = list(title = "Synthetic signal")) plotly_blechturm(p) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.column-margin} **Two renderers, one palette.** The static version remains useful in feeds and documents. Plotly provides inspection controls within this static website. ::: ## Market data from ledgr {#sec-market-data} These examples use an exported slice of **ledgr_demo_bars**, the bundled synthetic OHLCV dataset in the local ledgr repository. The seven source fields are `ts_utc`, `instrument_id`, `open`, `high`, `low`, `close`, and `volume`. The extract contains 60 observations for DEMO_01. The static comparisons show its last 30 rows. Prices and volumes come from the same observations in every chart. These are synthetic price units, with no corporate-action adjustment applied. The timestamps retain their UTC values. They are synthetic business-day labels at midnight, rather than exchange session-close timestamps. Calendar gaps remain visible; no missing bars are filled or assigned zero volume. [Download the source rows](data/ledgr-demo-bars.csv) or inspect the [source revision, generator, and file hashes](data/source.json). These are input-data visualizations; they do not describe a strategy's performance or execution fills. **Direction convention:** blue means close is greater than or equal to open; orange means close is below open. Equal open and close produce a horizontal doji body. Volume uses the same convention. ::: {.panel-tabset} ### OHLC bars The vertical stem runs from low to high. The left tick marks open; the right tick marks close. Volume sits below on the same timestamp axis. ::: {.plot-light} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_market_bars(visible_bars, style = "ohlc", mode = "light") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/market-ohlc-light-1.png){fig-alt='Thirty synthetic DEMO_01 OHLC bars with open ticks on the left and close ticks on the right, blue for up or flat and orange for down; volume is aligned beneath the prices on a light background.' width=768} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.plot-dark} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_market_bars(visible_bars, style = "ohlc", mode = "dark") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/market-ohlc-dark-1.png){fig-alt='The same thirty OHLC observations and aligned volume panel on a dark background.' width=768} ::: ::: ::: ### Filled candles The body spans open to close and the wick spans low to high. Both directions use filled bodies here. ::: {.plot-light} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_market_bars(visible_bars, style = "filled", mode = "light") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/market-filled-light-1.png){fig-alt='Thirty synthetic DEMO_01 filled candlesticks, blue for close at or above open and orange for close below open, with aligned volume on a light background.' width=768} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.plot-dark} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_market_bars(visible_bars, style = "filled", mode = "dark") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/market-filled-dark-1.png){fig-alt='The same thirty filled candlesticks and volume observations on a dark background.' width=768} ::: ::: ::: ### Hollow candles Up bodies are hollow with blue outlines; down bodies are filled orange. The hollow/filled distinction supplements color. ::: {.plot-light} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_market_bars(visible_bars, style = "hollow", mode = "light") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/market-hollow-light-1.png){fig-alt='Thirty synthetic DEMO_01 candles with hollow blue up bodies and filled orange down bodies, wicks for high and low, and aligned volume on a light background.' width=768} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.plot-dark} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_market_bars(visible_bars, style = "hollow", mode = "dark") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/market-hollow-dark-1.png){fig-alt='The same hollow and filled candlesticks with aligned volume on a dark background.' width=768} ::: ::: ::: ::: ### Interactive candles and volume {#sec-market-interactive} This chart contains all 60 source observations and initially displays the last 30. Hover over or tap a candle to inspect its OHLC values and volume. Zoom or pan to inspect the earlier observations. The price and volume panels share the UTC timestamp axis. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} market_candles_widget(market_bars, visible = 30) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Tables, static and interactive {#sec-tables} ::: {#tbl-summary .cell tbl-cap='Descriptive statistics for the synthetic observations.'} ```{.r .cell-code} summary_table <- data.frame( Statistic = c("Count", "Mean", "Standard deviation", "Minimum", "Maximum"), Value = c(nrow(research), mean(research$innovation), sd(research$innovation), min(research$innovation), max(research$innovation)) ) knitr::kable(summary_table, digits = 3, align = c("l", "r")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |Statistic | Value| |:------------------|-------:| |Count | 252.000| |Mean | -0.024| |Standard deviation | 0.974| |Minimum | -2.993| |Maximum | 2.702| ::: ::: @tbl-summary is a regular HTML table, suitable for copying and reading in RSS. ### An R htmlwidget This second table runs entirely in the browser after rendering. Try sorting a column, searching, or changing pages. It does not need an R server. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} DT::datatable( transform(research, innovation = round(innovation, 3), path = round(path, 3)), rownames = FALSE, class = "compact stripe hover", width = "100%", options = list(pageLength = 5, lengthChange = FALSE, scrollX = TRUE) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: A static table remains useful when an interactive widget is unavailable in a feed reader, PDF, or other non-browser output. ## Mathematics Inline mathematics, such as $\mu = 0$ and $\sigma = 1$, works within a sentence. A displayed equation can have its own label: $$ \bar{x} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i $$ {#eq-mean} @eq-mean defines the sample mean used in @tbl-summary. ## Tabs and columns ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Interpretation Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Morbi leo risus, porta ac consectetur ac, vestibulum at eros. Integer posuere erat a ante venenatis dapibus posuere velit aliquet. ### Method The inputs are synthetic normal draws with an explicit seed. This tab keeps a methodological aside close to the main text. ### Reproduction Render this article explicitly to rerun its R code: ```bash quarto render articles/quarto-showcase/index.qmd ``` ::: ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ### Lorem Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Donec sed odio dui. Nullam id dolor id nibh ultricies vehicula ut id elit. ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ### Ipsum Praesent commodo cursus magna, vel scelerisque nisl consectetur et. Maecenas sed diam eget risus varius blandit sit amet non magna. ::: ::: ## Callouts and disclosures ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## A collapsible explanation Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. This panel holds optional detail while leaving the main reading flow short. ::: ::: {.callout-important} ## A methodological assumption These data are synthetic. A layout demonstration is not evidence about a real process. ::: ::: {.callout-warning} ## A limitation This page demonstrates rendering features; it does not validate a model. ::: ::: {.callout-caution} ## A reproducibility reminder Frozen computation does not detect changes to external data or packages. Rerun the article explicitly when those inputs change. ::: ## A native diagram ```{mermaid} flowchart LR A["QMD source"] --> B["R execution"] B --> C["Frozen results"] C --> D["HTML article"] D --> E["Article listing and RSS"] ``` ## Citations and bibliography The citation @R comes from the local R installation's actual citation metadata.
